title: What Open Quantum Hardware Is
definition: Open Quantum Hardware: open-source quantum hardware.
description:
Strip Open Quantum Hardware to its essence and you get open-source quantum hardware. Simple to say, civilizational to build.

The path runs through Future Computing Paradigms: first open designs understanding, then hardware logistics prototypes, then fab access operations at scale. Each stage has its own physics, its own economics, and its own failure modes — this database maps all three.

Use the ladder: start with foundations, work through the components and forecasts, run every demo, then attempt the compounded drills. By the final record you will hold a working mental model of hardware hulls, grounded in real research and honest about what remains unknown.

t: Real Research Today: Open Quantum Hardware
title: Real Research Today: Open Quantum Hardware
definition: Today's documented research behind Open Quantum Hardware.
description:
The road to Open Quantum Hardware is already being paved. Intel's Loihi and IBM's TrueNorth/ NorthPole chips advance neuromorphic computing. Lightmatter and Luminous Computing build photonic AI accelerators.

Cerebras wafer-scale chips pack trillions of transistors for AI training. Together these programs form the open designs foundation that Open Quantum Hardware will build on — the hardware logistics results, the fab access methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as hardware logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

t: 2030 — First hardware hulls cloud instances rent open designs logic by
title: 2030 — First hardware hulls cloud instances rent open designs logic by
definition: 2030 milestone on the Open Quantum Hardware roadmap.
description:
First hardware hulls cloud instances rent open designs logic by the hour to researchers worldwide.

What must be true first: the open designs results have to replicate outside the lab, hardware logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and fab access operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed open designs demonstrations, hardware logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting fab access uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Open Quantum Hardware
definition: Estimates Open Quantum Hardware readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Open Quantum Hardware components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a hardware hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Open Quantum Hardware Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Open Quantum Hardware operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Open Quantum Hardware installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 37401 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where open designs monitoring, hardware logistics redundancy, or fab access maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Open Quantum Hardware Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Open Quantum Hardware: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Open Quantum Hardware — open-source quantum hardware.

Phase 1 — Prove (open designs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (hardware logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (fab access): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (community): hardware hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and research-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
